title: Menopause appointment
what: The doctor helps you go through menopause more comfortably. They look at hot flashes, sleep, and mood, and suggest treatment if needed.
why: For hot flashes, sweating, sleeplessness, mood swings, vaginal dryness, or irregular periods after age 40 to 45.
duration: the visit usually takes 30 to 40 minutes; test results come in 1 to 7 days
tell_doctor: What bothers you most: hot flashes, sleep, mood, dryness
Blood clots, or breast or uterine cancer, in you or relatives
High blood pressure, liver disease, or broken bones
What medicines and supplements you take

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: For a week, write down how often you have hot flashes and how you sleep.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring your latest mammogram, ultrasound, and test results, if you have them.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Think about what you want to discuss: hormones, bones, weight, sex.

bring: A list of your medicines and supplements
Your latest mammogram and test results
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms and health
Your blood pressure and weight are checked
A pelvic exam and breast exam are done
You get referrals: blood tests, ultrasound, mammogram, sometimes a bone density scan
The options are explained: lifestyle, hormones, and other medicines
feel: The pelvic exam may be uncomfortable with dryness. Tell your doctor
after: If treatment is prescribed, a follow-up is usually after 2 to 3 months
Exercise, not smoking, and a diet with calcium help your bones and heart
Have breast checks and smear tests regularly
red_flags: Bleeding after your periods have stopped for a year: see a doctor

faq.a: For many women, the benefits outweigh the risks if started at the right time. Your doctor will assess your risks.

faq.q: How long do hot flashes last?
faq.a: It varies, usually a few years. Treatment helps reduce them.

faq.q: Do I need birth control during menopause?
faq.a: Usually yes, until your periods have stopped for a year. Check with your doctor.

reminders.text: Menopause appointment tomorrow. Bring your latest mammogram, test results, and medicine list.
